intro: A scratchy, painful throat is one of the most common complaints we hear from travelers in Los Cabos. Dry airplane cabins, air-conditioned rooms, late nights, poolside drinks and shouting over music at a beach club can all leave your throat raw — and sometimes a virus or a bacterial infection like strep throat is behind it.

Most sore throats are caused by viruses and settle on their own within a few days. Others need a doctor, and a few need care right away. This guide explains the difference, what you can do to feel more comfortable, the warning signs not to ignore, and how to see an English-speaking doctor at your hotel, villa or yacht in Cabo San Lucas, the Tourist Corridor or San José del Cabo.

sections.h2: Common causes of a sore throat on vacation
list: Viral infections: colds, flu and other respiratory viruses are the most frequent cause, often with a runny nose, cough or hoarse voice.
Strep throat: a bacterial infection that is more common in children and teens but can affect adults, too.
Dry air: long flights and strong air conditioning dry out the throat, especially overnight.
Dehydration: sun, heat and alcohol leave you with less fluid than usual.
Irritation: cigarette or cigar smoke, loud talking or singing, and very cold or very spicy food and drinks.
Allergies and post-nasal drip: new surroundings, dust or pool chemicals can trigger mucus that irritates the throat.

sections.h2: Strep throat vs. a viral sore throat
p: Only an exam — and often a quick throat test — can tell for sure, but some patterns are typical:

h3.h: Signs that can point to strep
list: Sudden, intense throat pain and pain when swallowing
Fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher
Red, swollen tonsils, sometimes with white patches or streaks of pus
Tiny red spots on the roof of the mouth
Swollen, tender glands in the front of the neck
Headache, stomach ache or nausea, especially in children
Usually no cough or runny nose

h3.h: Signs that point more to a virus
list: Cough, sneezing, runny or stuffy nose
Hoarse voice
Red, watery eyes
Gradual onset along with general cold or flu symptoms

p_after: Strep is treated with prescription antibiotics, while viral sore throats are not helped by antibiotics. That is why guessing — or taking leftover pills from home — is not a good idea. A doctor can examine you, decide whether testing makes sense and recommend the right treatment.

sections.h2: What you can do to feel more comfortable
p: These general steps can ease discomfort while you rest or arrange a visit. They do not replace medical care:
list: Drink plenty of fluids — bottled or purified water, warm tea, broth or electrolyte drinks.
Rest your voice and skip the loud bars for a night or two.
Gargle with warm salt water a few times a day (adults and older children who can gargle safely).
Add moisture to the air: turn the air conditioning down a little at night, or take a steamy shower.
Choose soft, soothing foods and avoid alcohol, smoke and very spicy or acidic dishes.

Ask before taking anything. Check with a doctor or pharmacist before using pain relievers, throat lozenges or sprays, especially for children, during pregnancy, or if you take other medication or have health conditions.
p_after: Remember that in Mexico antibiotics are sold with a prescription. A short visit is the quickest way to get the right one if you need it.

sections.h2: When to see a doctor — and when to call 911
p: Arrange a doctor visit the same day if you have:
list: Fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher with a sore throat
White patches on the tonsils or swollen, tender neck glands
A sore throat that is severe, getting worse, or lasting more than a few days
A rash along with a sore throat and fever
Pain on one side of the throat with difficulty opening your mouth or a muffled voice
A sore throat in a child, an older adult, someone pregnant, or anyone with a weakened immune system
Little or no urination, dizziness or other signs of dehydration because swallowing hurts
p_after: Call 911 right away if you or someone with you has trouble breathing or noisy breathing, cannot swallow saliva or is drooling, has swelling of the tongue, lips, face or neck, cannot open the mouth, is confused or extremely drowsy, or has a stiff neck with a high fever. These can be signs of a serious infection, an allergic reaction or an airway problem that needs emergency care.

sections.h2: Seeing a doctor in Cabo without leaving your room

p: An English-speaking doctor comes to your hotel, villa or yacht 24/7, reviews your symptoms, examines your throat, ears and glands, and prescribes treatment if appropriate. Typical arrival is 30–45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas and the Tourist Corridor, and up to about 60 minutes in San José del Cabo, Pedregal and Palmilla. Book a house-call doctor.
Staying near downtown? You can be seen at our clinic on Francisco I. Madero, Centro, Cabo San Lucas, for $99 USD.
Prescriptions, throat lozenges, bottled water and electrolytes can be delivered to your room 24/7 — free over $50 USD (a fee may apply between 10 PM and 7 AM). Order pharmacy delivery.

p_after: There is no payment before the visit, and you receive an itemized invoice in English and USD for your travel insurance (US and Canadian insurance accepted, subject to verification). See every rate on our prices page.

sections.h2: When the whole group is run down
p: Sore throats tend to travel through families and friend groups sharing a villa. If several people are feeling drained and dehydrated, the doctor can see everyone during the same visit. For general fluid and wellness support, an IV drip such as Immunity Armor ($159 at your door) is an option some travelers choose after a doctor confirms it is appropriate — it is not a treatment for strep or any infection. Groups of 6 or more can book group IV therapy at $119 USD per person, tax included.

sections.h2: Tips to protect your throat for the rest of your trip
list: Carry a refillable bottle of purified water and sip through the day.
Alternate alcoholic drinks with water, especially in the sun.
Set the air conditioning a few degrees warmer at night.
Wash hands often and avoid sharing cups, straws and utensils.
Give your voice a break after loud nights out.
If you are prescribed antibiotics, take them exactly as directed and finish the course.
p_after: For other common vacation illnesses and how to get help fast, read our guide on what to do if you get sick in Cabo.

faq.q: Can I get antibiotics for strep throat without a prescription in Cabo?
faq.a: In Mexico, antibiotics are sold with a prescription. A doctor visit at your hotel ($189 USD) or at our clinic ($99 USD) lets you get examined and, if appropriate, prescribed treatment the same day, which we can deliver to your room.

faq.q: How do I know if my sore throat is strep?
faq.a: Sudden throat pain, fever, swollen tonsils with white patches and tender neck glands without a cough are typical of strep, but only an exam and testing can confirm it. A doctor can check you and recommend the right treatment.

faq.q: How quickly can a doctor come to my hotel in Cabo?
faq.a: Our English-speaking doctors are available 24/7. Typical arrival is 30 to 45 minutes in Cabo San Lucas and the Tourist Corridor, and up to about 60 minutes in San José del Cabo, Pedregal and Palmilla.

faq.q: Will travel insurance reimburse a sore throat visit?
faq.a: Many travel insurance plans reimburse doctor visits abroad. You pay after the visit and receive an itemized invoice in English and USD to submit to your insurer. We accept international health and travel insurance from the United States and Canada, subject to policy verification and coverage confirmation.

faq.q: When is a sore throat an emergency?
faq.a: Call 911 for trouble breathing, drooling or inability to swallow saliva, swelling of the face, tongue or neck, inability to open the mouth, confusion, or a stiff neck with high fever.
